title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: A system uses a language model to help with a task. Which question best tells you whether it is a workflow or an agent?

options.text: Whether the system has any tools it can use to take actions
Whether the model has a large enough context window for the task
Whether the program's code or the model decides what happens next
Whether the system calls the model more than once per request

items.stem: A program always calls the model exactly three times, in the same order: first to pull the machine and date out of a booking request, then to draft a reply, then to polish the reply. The model never chooses which step comes next. True or false: this system is an agent.
When the steps of a task are known in advance, a fixed workflow is often a better choice than an agent. Name two reasons, in one or two sentences.
Which of these tasks most needs an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Booking a machine slot by always checking the calendar, then the training record, then booking
Sending every student the same confirmation message once a booking is made
Pulling the machine name and date out of each incoming booking request
Finding why a student's 3D prints keep failing, where each next check depends on the last result

items.stem: For your makerspace assistant, a booking request always needs the same three checks in the same order: calendar free, student trained, then book. Your sponsor's model budget is small. Which design is best for this part, judged by cost and predictability?

options.text: Code that runs the three steps in that order, using the model only to read the request and write the reply
An agent with three tools, so the model can handle unusual requests in whatever order they need
An agent with three tools and a high step limit, so it is allowed to finish every booking
An agent with three tools, because any system that takes real actions has to run as a loop

items.stem: A teammate proposes this fixed design for answering manual questions: the code runs search_manuals once with the student's words, then the model writes an answer from the results. Student questions vary: some need one page, some need two manuals compared, and some need a second search with different words. What is the main weakness of the design?

options.text: Every request pays for a search, so it costs more than an agent would
It is not really a workflow, because the model writes the final answer
The code cannot adapt: if the first search misses, nothing decides to search again
It will keep repeating the search forever unless a step limit is added
